newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian rupiah recoups loss, liquidity volatile.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian rupiah recoups loss, liquidity volatile.

text.p: The Indonesian rupiah recouped losses against the dollar in late trading on Friday.
Dealers said the rupiah bounced back to 2,374.0/76.0 at 0845 GMT after falling to a low of 2,380.0.
They said local nervousness over unfounded rumours of trouble in the west Java city of Bandung stirred a sensitive market after riots hit Rengasdengklok, east of Jakarta, on Thursday.
A mob of Indonesian Moslems burned and wrecked churches and temples at Rengasdengklok after reports that a Christian had insulted Islam, officials said.
Dealers said, however, the rupiah regained some ground after realising the Bandung rumours were unfounded.
One currency dealer in Singapore said there was also some spillover from the Thai Baht which was hit by offshore players.
"It's just the timing which causes increased pressure on the rupiah. Fund managers are using the chance to square and drive the rupiah down to a low of 2,380.0," he said.
Dealers said the sensitive market was also depressed by criticism from the U.S. overnight on human rights in East Timor, putting additional pressure on the rupiah.
Dealers said, however, local operators seemed to have won the battle for now as they stayed calm and fought back against the offshore attack by raising swap costs.
"I think we have won the muscle play at present. Fund managers seem to have reversed positions after being squeezed by expensive swaps," one U.S. bank dealer said.
He said offshore players were forced to unload dollars and thus liquidate their swap holdings, causing swap premiums and interbank rates to ease across the board.
Tomorrow and today rupiah closed at 2,375.0/75.5 and 2,375.0/76.0, respectively.
Another dealer said tight liquidity following weekly tax payments and the month-end and weekend factors helped remind operators to be careful with the expensive rupiah.
The U.S. bank dealer said there were also rumours that some big sellers were positioned at the 2,380.0 level, which also kept the dollar from going higher.
Overnight money soared to a high of 27 percent before it settled at 14.0/15.0 percent late in the afternoon.
Dealers said differing anticipation of liquidity seemed to have caused a relative volatility in the market on Friday.
Overnight swaps were at 3.0/3.3. Tom/next swaps eased to 0.8/1.0 after rising to a high of 1.75 points.
One-month swaps declined to 14.75 from 17.00, three to 39.0 from 41.0 and six to 78.0/80.0 from 82.0/83.0 points.
The central bank raised its intervention band by one point to 2,372/2,564 and the conversion band also by one point to 2,372/2,420 on Friday, the third increase this week.
The central bank depreciated the rupiah by two points last week after lowering it by four points the previous week.
